questions.stem: All Trans’ retinoic acid is used in the treatment of tumor associated with?
questions.solutionHtml:
PML-RARA
  • All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) is used in the treatment of tumors associated with B. PML-RARA.
  • PML-RARA is a fusion gene resulting from a chromosomal translocation between the PML gene on chromosome 15 and the RARA gene on chromosome 17.
  • This translocation is characteristic of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
  • ATRA is a derivative of vitamin A and acts as a differentiating agent in APL treatment. It binds to the abnormal PML-RARA protein, promoting the differentiation of leukemia cells into mature granulocytes, and inducing remission in APL patients.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 622-624

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman came with complaints of easy fatigability, exertion dyspnea and weight loss. She also complaints of Frequent fall. Physical Examination revealed there was bilateral decrease in vibration sense. Her hemoglobin levels were 8.2gm%. She was treated with folate. Her anemia improved but neurological symptoms worsened. Which of the following is the most probable reason for her condition?

options.label: C
options.text: Deficiency of folate reductase in CNS

options.label: D
options.text: Folate therapy caused rapid use of B12 Stores aggravating Symptoms

questions.answerText: Folate therapy caused rapid use of B12 Stores aggravating Symptoms
questions.solutionHtml:
Folate therapy caused rapid use of B12 Stores aggravating Symptoms

Vitamin B12

  • The most probable reason for the worsening of neurological symptoms in this patient despite the improvement of anemia with folate therapy is D. Folate therapy caused rapid use of B12 stores aggravating symptoms.

questions.stem: A 25- year- old man presents for a routine physical examination. The patient is tall (6ft, 5in) and on examination he was found to have an early diastolic murmur. Which of the following is the mode of inheritance by which the disease is likely to be transmitted?
questions.solutionHtml:
AD
  • The patient's tall stature (6ft, 5in) and the presence of an early diastolic murmur are suggestive of Marfan syndrome, which is a genetic disorder affecting connective tissue.
  • Marfan syndrome is primarily inherited in an autosomal dominant (AD) manner, caused by mutations in the FBN1 gene on chromosome 15.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors play a major role in initiation of thrombus formation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Endothelial injury
  • The major factor that plays a key role in the initiation of thrombus formation is D. Endothelial injury.
  • The endothelium is the inner lining of blood vessels and serves as a protective barrier between the blood and the vessel wall. When the endothelium is damaged due to various reasons, such as trauma, inflammation, or atherosclerosis, it exposes the underlying subendothelial tissue.
  • The exposed subendothelial tissue contains collagen and other procoagulant substances that are usually not in contact with circulating blood. Once exposed, these substances trigger platelet activation and the coagulation cascade.

questions.stem: 33-year-old man presents with a 5-week history of calf pain and swelling and low-grade fever. Serum levels of creatine kinase are elevated. A Muscle biopsy reveals numerous eosinophils. He also has peripheral blood eosinophilia. Which of the following interleukins is primarily responsible for the increase in eosinophils in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
IL4
  • The interleukin primarily responsible for the increase in eosinophils in this patient is B. IL-4.
  • Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell involved in the immune response, particularly against parasitic infections and allergic reactions. Interleukins are signaling proteins that play a crucial role in regulating the immune system and inflammation.
  • IL-4 is known as an interleukin-4 and is produced by T helper 2 (Th2) cells and mast cells. It is a key cytokine involved in promoting the differentiation and activation of eosinophils.
  • IL-4 stimulates the production and release of eosinophils from the bone marrow and enhances their survival in peripheral tissues.
  • Additionally, IL-4 also induces the expression of cell surface receptors on eosinophils, making them more responsive to other proinflammatory signals. 

Note:- Most potent activator of eosinophil is  IL5 > IL4

So, best answer is IL4 here.

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year old person who is chronic smoker came to the clinic with Complaints of cough. The physician examines the patient and take a biopsy. The picture in the biopsy was as the description below. Which of the following cellular changes has happened in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metaplasia
  • Here, the picture shows normal pseudostratified epithelium is replaced by squamous epithelium which suggests the diagnosis of Squamous Metaplasia.
  • Metaplasia is a reversible change in which one differentiated cell type is replaced by another cell type that is not normally present in that tissue.

questions.stemHtml: A 5-year old male child presented to the clinic with history of recurrent infections. On Examination the child had Rashes as shown below. Routine blood investigations revealed the patient had low platelets. Which of the following is the probable diagnosis in the kid?
questions.solutionHtml:
Wiskott Aldrich syndrome
  • The description of a 5-year-old male child presenting with recurrent infections, rashes, and low platelets suggests the probable diagnosis of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the Correct Statement related to Huntington’s Chorea?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a trinucleotide Expansion mutation related disorder

options.label: B
options.text: There are abnormal repeats of CUG

options.label: D
options.text: Abnormality is seen due to mutation in Chromosome 6

questions.answerText: It is a trinucleotide Expansion mutation related disorder
questions.solutionHtml:
It is a trinucleotide Expansion mutation related disorder
  • The correct statement related to Huntington's Chorea is- It is a trinucleotide Expansion mutation-related disorder.
  • Huntington's Chorea is a neurodegenerative disorder caused by an expansion of the CAG trinucleotide repeat in the HTT gene.
  • This expansion leads to the production of an abnormal form of the huntingtin protein, resulting in the characteristic symptoms and pathology of Huntington's Chorea.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old-boy presents with complaints of fatigue and abdominal pain after playing football. On detailed history taking he also complaints of painful swelling of digits in the past. On USG of abdomen he was found to have small spleen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sickle cell anemia
  • Based on the provided information, the most likely diagnosis for the 10-year-old boy with complaints of fatigue, abdominal pain after playing football, painful swelling of digits in the past, and a small spleen on abdominal ultrasound is: B. Sickle cell anemia

questions.stemHtml: A 25-year-old male presented with a 2cm thyroid nodule. A thyroidectomy was done. The histology picture is given bellow. What could be the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Papillary Carcinoma Thyroid
  • The given clinical scenario and histopathological image showing papillary architecture, where the tumor cells form finger-like projections or papillae and orphan Annie’s eye nuclei suggests the diagnosis of papillary carcinoma thyroid.
  • It accounts for approximately 80% of all thyroid cancers.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old came with complaints of thyroid swelling. On investigations her TSH levels were found to be elevated. Post-Operative HPE reports Showed lymphocytic infiltration and Hurthle cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hashimoto thyroiditis
  • The given clinical scenario including the complaint of thyroid swelling, elevated TSH levels, and the histopathological findings of lymphocytic infiltration and Hurthle cells, suggests the diagnosis of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
  • It is an autoimmune condition that causes inflammation of the thyroid gland.

questions.stem: Loss of foot process is classical is case of?
questions.solutionHtml:
Minimal change disease
  • Loss of foot processes is classical in the case of B. Minimal change disease.
  • Three hallmarks of minimal change disease are:-
    • Diffuse loss of Podocyte foot processes
    • Vacuolation, and
    • Appearance of microvilli



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 555

questions.stem: A 51-year-old person came with complaints of hematuria to the clinic. On examination he was normotensive and had pedal edema. Investigations revealed the patient had nor glycosuria and had a creatinine value of 9. Which of the following investigations one should do to identify the etiology of the disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anti GBM antibodies
  • The combination of hematuria, pedal edema, and elevated creatinine is suggestive of Goodpasture’s syndrome.
  • Goodpasture’s syndrome is characterized by acute renal failure due to RPGN and pulmonary haemorrhage.
  • The evidence in support are the characteristic linear deposits of anti-GBM antibodies consisting of IgG and complement along the GBM, detection of circulating anti-GBM antibodies.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 701

questions.stem: Which of the following disease will have irregular, bulky, and friable cardiac vegetations?
questions.solutionHtml:
Infective Endocarditis
  • The disease that will have irregular, bulky, and friable cardiac vegetations is: B. Infective Endocarditis.
  • The cardiac vegetations in infective endocarditis are composed of fibrin, platelets, microorganisms, and inflammatory cells.
  • These vegetation can vary in size, shape, and appearance but are often described as irregular, bulky, and friable.

questions.stem: Which of the following will be seen on cardiac biopsy of a patient who had post MI reperfusion injury?
questions.solutionHtml:
Eosinophilic contraction bands
  • Post-MI reperfusion injury refers to the damage that can occur to cardiac muscle when blood flow is restored after a period of ischemia (lack of blood flow) during a myocardial infarction.
  • During the process of reperfusion, there is an influx of calcium ions into the injured myocardial cells, leading to the formation of eosinophilic bands known as "eosinophilic contraction bands."

questions.stem: A 20-year-old presented with swelling in the wrist joint for 2 years duration. HPE showed spindle shaped cells and Verocay bodies. Which of the following is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Schwannoma
  • The given clinical scenario and histopathological image showing Verocay bodies suggests the diagnosis of
  • It is an encapsulated, solid, sometimes cystic, tumour that produces eccentric enlargement of the nerve root from where it arises.

questions.stemHtml: A 35-year-old heterosexual patient diagnosed with HIV had history of chronic watery diarrhea. Colonoscopy biopsy is shown as below. Which of the following is your most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryptosporidium
  • The given clinical scenario of diarrhea in an HIV positive patient and colonic biopsy showing uniformly stained acid-fast oocyst suggests the diagnosis of Cryptosporidium infection.
  • It is a protozoan parasite that can cause gastrointestinal infections, particularly in individuals with compromised immune systems, such as those with HIV/AIDS.
  • It is known to cause chronic watery diarrhea in immunocompromised indivisuals.

questions.stemHtml: A 5-year old kid presented with history of blood in stools. On examination there was a Polypoidal mass in rectum, biopsy of which is shown as below. Your most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Juvenile polyp
  • The given clinical history and a histopathological image showing dilated glands filled with mucin is suggestive of a Juvenile polyp (retention polyps).
  • Juvenile polyps are the most common type of colorectal polyps in children, and they are usually pedunculated with a smooth surface.
  • Usually <3cm in diameter
  • Histologically, they are characterized by cystically dilated glands lined by normal-appearing epithelium.
  • These polyps are benign and usually do not require any further intervention after polypectomy.

questions.stem: A 30 year old male came with complaints of swelling around the knee joint. Histopathological examination of the swelling demonstrated many giant cells interspersed with mono-nuclear cells. Your most probable diagnosis is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Giant cell tumor
  • The most probable diagnosis based on the histopathological examination of the swelling with many giant cells interspersed with mono-nuclear cells is: D. Giant cell tumor.
  • The tumour arises in the epiphysis of long bones close to the articular cartilage.
  • Most common sites of involvement are lower end of femur and upper end of tibia (i.e. about the knee), lower end of radius and upper end of fibula.
  • The hallmark features of giant cell tumour are the presence of large number of multinucleate osteoclast like giant cells regularly scattered throughout the stromal mononuclear cells

questions.stem: A 40-years old person presented with 10x8cm swelling in retro peritoneum. Molecular analysis demonstrated t(12,16). Which of the following is your most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Myxoid liposarcoma
  • Liposarcoma: Most common sarcomas of adulthood
  • Seen mainly in 50s to 60s in the deep soft tissues of the proximal extremities and in the retroperitoneum.
  • Amplification of 12q13-ql 5 and t(12;16) are characteristic of well-differentiated and myxoid liposarcomas, respectively.
  • Key genes: chromosome 12q is MDM2, which is a potent inhibitor of p53
  • Contains adipocytes with scattered atypical spindle cells.
  • Myxoid liposarcoma has abundant basophilic extracellular matrix, arborizing capillaries and primitive cells reminiscent of fetal fat.
  • Pleomorphic liposarcoma consists of sheets of anaplastic cells, bizarre nuclei and variable amounts of lipoblasts.
  • The pleomorphic variant of liposarcoma is usually aggressive and frequently metastasizes.

questions.stem: A 20- year-old presented to the clinic with history of malabsorption, diarrhea and poor appetite, Vomiting, poor appetite. Duodenal Biopsy of the patient showed crypt hyperplasia, villi atrophy, CD8+ Cells in lamina propria. Your most probable diagnosis is.
questions.solutionHtml:
Celiac disease
  • The given clinical scenario with history of malabsorption, diarrhoea and duodenal biopsy showing crypt hyperplasia, villi atrophy, and CD8+ cells in the lamina propria suggests the diagnosis of Celiac disease.
  • It is an autoimmune disorder characterized by an immune reaction to gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye.
  • It primarily affects the small intestine, leading to inflammation, villous atrophy, and crypt hyperplasia.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presented to the clinic with a 4cm mass in the upper outer quadrant. Biopsy bland nuclei and mucin infiltrating the stroma. Which of the following is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Colloid carcinoma
  • Colloid carcinoma AKA mucinous carcinoma
  • Colloid carcinoma is seen in about 2% cases, occurs more frequently in older women and is slow-growing.
  • Colloid carcinoma has better prognosis than the usual infiltrating duct carcinoma.
  • Grossly- The tumour is usually a soft and gelatinous mass with well-demarcated borders.
  • Colloid carcinoma contains large amount of extracellular epithelial mucin and acini filled with mucin. Cuboidal to tall columnar tumour cells, some showing mucus vacuolation, are seen floating in large lakes of mucin.
  • Abundant mucin production is not a feature of other choices.

questions.stemHtml: A 35 year-old woman with a long history of dyspnea, chronic cough, sputum production, and wheezing dies of respiratory failure following a bout of pneumonia. She was not a smoker or alcoholic. The lung at autopsy is shown in the image. Which of the following underlying Conditions was most likely associated with the pathologic changes shown here?
questions.solutionHtml:
Alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency
  • The given clinical scenario with the history of dyspnea, chronic cough, sputum production, wheezing, and the image showing emphysematous lungs suggests the diagnosis of Alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency causing Emphysema.
  • In individuals with alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency, the lack of this protective protein leads to uncontrolled activity of Elastase enzymes, resulting in tissue damage, particularly in the lungs.

questions.stem: A 23 year old male presented to the clinic with history of Fatigue and tiredness. On investigation he was found to have Hb values of -9gm%, MCV OF 101 FL. Peripheral smear examination showed macrocytic RBC and hypersegmented neutrophils. Which of the following is the most likely etiology?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chronic alcoholism
  • MCV – 101fl is suggestive of macrocytosis
  • most commonly (especially when the increase in size is mild, and just above normal range) the cause is bone marrow dysplasia secondary to alcohol abuse and chronic alcoholism, Poor absorption of vitamin B12 in the digestive tract can also cause macrocytosis.
  • Macrocytosis is frequently linked to alcoholism, with or without liver disease. In fact, it is purported to be one of the most common causes of non megaloblastic macrocytosis
  • In cases of macrocytosis related to alcoholism the elevated MCV may be due to the direct effect of the alcohol, liver disease and/or folate deficiency.

questions.stem: Which of the following infection is common within 1- 4 months post transplant?
questions.solutionHtml:
CMV
  • Transplant patients are among those most vulnerable to CMV infection, especially in the critical few months after the transplant.
  • Between 20% and 60% of people with a solid organ transplant develop a symptomatic CMV infection. These symptoms are similar to the flu – fever, body aches, sore throat – and may be difficult to control.
  • The disease caused by post-transplant CMV (PT-CMV) occurs due to:-
    • Transmission from the transplanted organ,
    • Due to reactivation of latent infection, or
    • After a primary infection in seronegative transplant patients.
